name: Sika Concrete Fix
paste:
SIKA® CONCRETE FIX: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Concrete Fix, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/b/sika-concrete-fix.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Concrete Fix where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Concrete Fix is a 2-component, 100% solids, moisture-tolerant, high-modulus, high-strength, structural, smooth-paste epoxy adhesive. (Sika® Concrete Fix is also known as Sikadur-33)
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - As a structural adhesive for.
    - Concrete elements
    - Hard natural stone
    - Ceramics, fibre cement
    - Mortar, Bricks, Blocks, Masonry, render etc.
    - Steel, Iron, Aluminium
    - Wood
    - Polyester, Epoxy
    - Corners and edges
    - Hole and void filling
    - Joint arrises
    For concrete repairs
    Interior, vertical and overhead repair of:
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Joint filling and crack sealing.
    - Crack filling and sealing (non moving)
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Metalwork, carpentry.
    - Fixing and fastening of handrails, railings, balustrades and supports
    - Fixing of window and door frames
1.6 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - For use in the following.
    - Concrete
    - Hard natural stone
    - Solid rock
    - Hollow and solid masonry
    - Steel
    - Wood
1.7 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Concrete Fix
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: High Modulus, High-Strength, Structural, Rapid Curing Epoxy, Smooth-Paste Adhesive
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates. AS4020:2018 approved for use in potable Water applications.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 12614: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Heat deflection temperature (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Can be used on damp concrete
    - Excellent adhesion to the substrate
    - Non-sag, also overhead
    - High load capacity
    - Shrinkage-free hardening
    - Styrene-free
    - Convenient easy mix ratio A : B = 1 : 1 by volume
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Colour: Concrete grey
    - Density: 1.35 kg/litre (part A+B mixed)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Consistency: Smooth-paste adhesive
    - Compressive strength: ~ 50 N/mm2 (14 days + 23oC)
    - Tensile strength: 10-15 MPa (14 days at +23 oC)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 9.3x10⁻⁵per oC (Temp. range +23 oC - +60 oC) (EN 1770)
    - Heat deflection temperature: +49 oC (7 days at +23oC) (EN 12614)
2.7 Tensile adhesion strength.
    | Time | Substrate | Bond Strength |
    | After 3 days | Dry Concrete | > 5 N/mm2 * |
    | After 3 days | Damp Concrete | > 5 N/mm2 * |
    | After 3 days | Steel Blast cleaned | > 10 N/mm² |
    | After 3 days | Brick Dry | > 1.5 N/mm2 ** |
    * 100% concrete failure
    ** 100% brick failure
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 1 litre kit
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days. Adequate substrate strength (concrete, masonry, natural stone) must always be confirmed.
3.3 Substrate preparation. Surface must be clean and sound. It may be dry or damp, but free from standing water. Remove dust, laitance, grease, curing compounds, impregnations, waxes and any other contaminants.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Preparation Work.
    - Concrete, natural stone, cement mortar and render: Clean, free from oils and grease, no loose or friable particles, no cement laitance.
    - Age of concrete 3 to 6 weeks (dependent on mix design and environment). Preparation: Blastcleaning or grinding.
    - Construction steel 37, V2 A steel: Free from oil, grease, rust or mill scale. Preparation: Blastcleaning or grinding. Avoid dew point conditions. If prepared steel is not to be used immediately, its surface must be coated with Sikagard®-62 to protect it.
3.5 Substrate preparation - Polyester, epoxy, ceramics.
    - Free from oils and grease. Polyester epoxy: Grind, using coarse abrasive.
    - Glass, ceramics: Grinding, do not apply to siliconised substrates.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: A : B = 1 : 1 by volume
    - Consumption: 1 litre/m² per mm of thickness
    - Layer thickness: 0.5mm min. / 10mm max.
    - Pot Life: 60 minutes (+23 oC)
4.3 Curing time.
    | Temperature | Open Time | Curing Time |
    | +10 oC | 210 minutes | 3 days * |
    | +20 oC | 90 minutes | 2 days * |
    | +35 oC | 45 minutes | 1 day * |
    * To achieve approx. 80% of the performance
4.4 Mixing. Pre-mix each component. Proportion equal parts by volume of Component ‘B’ and Component ‘A’ into a clean pail. Mix thoroughly for 3 minutes with Sika paddle on low speed (400-600 rpm) drill until uniform in colour. Mix only the quantity that can be used within its potlife.
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Apply Sika® Concrete Fix to the prepared substrate by trowel or gloved hand. Ensure the material is worked well (scrubbed) into the surface, this is particularly important on damp surfaces. There should be no standing water on concrete surfaces. If using Sika® Concrete Fix as an adhesive, coat both adherents and press into place (on vertical and overhead surfaces temporary support must be provided). The adhesive layer should not be less than 2 mm.
    - To seal injection ports and crack for injection grouting – Place the neat mixed material over the cracks to be pressure-injected and around each injection port. Allow sufficient time to set before pressure-injecting. Use Sikadur-52 Normal for the low-viscosity injection adhesive. Consult the Technical Data Sheet on this product for more information. Also contact Technical Services for additional information on pressure-injection grouting.
    - To anchor bolts, dowels, pins – Annular space around bolt should not exceed 3 mm, depth of embedment is typically 10-15 times the bolt diameter. Grout with neat Sika® Concrete Fix.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Uncured material may be cleaned from application tools, etc. by using Sika Colma Cleaner (flammable solvent). Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Minimum substrate and ambient temperature 4ºC
    - Do not thin. Addition of solvents will prevent proper cure.
    - Material is a vapour barrier after cure
    - Not for sealing and cracks under hydrostatic pressure at the time of application

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 85% max. (at +25 °C)
5.4 Dew point. Avoid condensation during dew point conditions. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3°C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Can be damp but not “wet”. No free standing water during application and curing.
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - Minimum substrate and ambient temperature 4ºC
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 9.3x10⁻⁵per oC (Temp. range +23 oC - +60 oC) (EN 1770)
    - Heat deflection temperature: +49 oC (7 days at +23oC) (EN 12614)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Concrete Fix, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/b/sika-concrete-fix.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® ConcreteFix Part A, version 10/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/f/sds-sika-concretefixparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) ontaining physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
